reason: Matches author-provided layout in the current Appendix A typography, with evidence-backed semantic corrections.
claim: Three commitments in job recovery. The Redis lease records in-flight work by job ID and issue epoch; it does not identify an owning worker. A database compare-and-set protects acquisition of the selected merge claim, while publication persists the artifact before updating durable job state. The inline path bypasses that merge claim. These operations cross separate stores; recovery and assurance address their different failure windows.
topology: A document job enters an in-flight accounting lease in Redis, storing job ID and issue epoch, not worker identity. The inline chunkless path bypasses the protected merge claim; the merge path must win a database compare-and-set. Both paths persist the artifact before updating durable job state and reaching completed or failed status. A separate recovery panel distinguishes stale-lease reissue, guarded stale release, interrupted effects, and interrupted publication. Three assurance rows distinguish the runtime claim constraint, bounded interleaving exploration, and temporal delivery and sweep assumptions.
